clue.text: Oddly dour and filthy place needing a clean

blocks.note: D and U, the odd letters of DOUR
a pigsty, the byword for a filthy place

explanation.surface: A grim, grubby room that badly wants cleaning.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the tail of the clue, not 'filthy place': STY takes those words, and 'needing a clean' is what the whole answer means.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dusty is covered in dust and so needs cleaning.

clue.text: Standard three consecutive notes you put in key

indicators.note: to put something in is to insert it

blocks.note: D, E and F follow each other in the musical scale
the Alt key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: A music lesson: play three notes in a row in the usual key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' and 'notes' both push towards music, but the key here is the one on a keyboard, ALT.
explanation.definitionFit: The default setting is the standard one used unless you change it.

clue.text: Demanding character, most often seen in casinos, flusters, getting worried

blocks.clueFragment: character, most often seen in casinos
blocks.note: S appears twice in CASINOS, more than any other letter

explanation.surface: A gambler flustered and anxious in the casino.
explanation.walkthrough: The S is found by counting: every other letter of CASINOS occurs once, S twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of taxing: a demanding boss or schedule puts you under strain.

clue.text: Baby wildebeest rears up beneath you when its tail gets pulled

blocks.clueFragment: you when its tail gets pulled

explanation.surface: A wildebeest calf bucks and kicks when someone yanks its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Baby wildebeest' looks like one phrase, but only 'Baby' is the definition; the animal is GNU.
explanation.definitionFit: Young as an adjective means baby, as in young animals.

clue.text: Procedure Committee’s leader enthralled by rendition of Queen hit

explanation.surface: A committee chair is spellbound by a cover of a Queen song.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital Q in 'Queen hit' makes it look like the band's song, but it is just letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A technique is a method or procedure for doing something.

clue.text: Rubbish farm vehicle reverses into another

definitions.note: 'another' means another farm vehicle, leaning on the phrase earlier in the clue

blocks.note: a cart is a farm vehicle

explanation.surface: A farm cart backs into another vehicle and makes a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the single word 'another': one farm vehicle, reversed, turns into another one.
explanation.definitionFit: A tractor is another farm vehicle besides the cart.

clue.text: Fuss created when the tip of red crayon’s broken

indicators.note: a tip is the very end of something
the letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A child throws a tantrum when their red crayon snaps.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's tantrum is the answer itself; 'broken' reads as the snapped crayon but tells you to rearrange the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: British informal: a carry-on is a needless to-do, an over-the-top fuss.

clue.text: Covering low ground, headless horsemen who operate in darkness

definitions.note: the definition is a relative clause standing for 'people who operate in darkness'

explanation.surface: Headless horsemen of legend ride across the lowlands by night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low ground' reads as a single phrase for a valley, but 'ground' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Night owls are people who are active late at night.

clue.text: During panel show, you and I forgot to say jokes

blocks.note: QI is a British TV comedy quiz panel show
a PS (postscript) is what you add when you forgot something

explanation.surface: A comedian on a TV panel show forgets to deliver the jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You and I' looks like one unit, but only 'you' goes inside the show; 'I forgot' is a PS.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a quip is a quick witty one-liner, the kind of joke a panellist throws in.

clue.text: Article in La Vanguardia on EE receiving tax boost

blocks.note: el is the Spanish for 'the'; La Vanguardia is a Spanish newspaper
the letters as written, split round the tax
value added tax, the UK sales tax

explanation.surface: A Spanish newspaper article about the phone firm EE getting a tax break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' in the newspaper sense is misdirection: it is a grammatical article, Spanish EL. EE is a British mobile network.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean lift up, literally or in status: you can boost or elevate a person's standing.

clue.text: Generate means with supporting capital from Man U and City

definitions.note: a formula is a means of generating a result

blocks.note: if you are for something, you support it

explanation.surface: Football finance: how Manchester United and City raise money from investors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man U' and 'City' look like the two Manchester clubs, but they split apart: M, U, and LA as the city.
explanation.definitionFit: A formula is a set method, a means of producing an outcome.

clue.text: Music college’s period of charity fundraising?

blocks.note: surface padding tying the rag to student life
rag is the annual student charity fundraising event at British universities and colleges

explanation.surface: A college's music department runs its charity week.
explanation.walkthrough: RAG week is a British student tradition of stunts and collections for charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragtime is the syncopated piano music of Scott Joplin's era.

clue.text: Repulsive, thin and ugly drunk devours seconds

indicators.note: to devour is to swallow whole

explanation.surface: An ugly drunk wolfs down second helpings.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'and' in 'thin and ugly' is part of the surface only; it joins the two fodder words.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsightly is unpleasant to look at, repulsive.

clue.text: When cycling, knock car

blocks.note: to slate is to criticise, knock

explanation.surface: A cyclist gets knocked off by a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' fits the road-accident picture so well that it reads as a bike, not as an instruction to rotate the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A brand name defined by its category: Tesla makes electric cars, and a Tesla is one of them.

clue.text: Express disapproval about fellow close to Scooby — Shaggy?

blocks.note: tut is the clicking sound of disapproval

explanation.surface: Tutting at Scooby-Doo's scruffy sidekick Shaggy.
explanation.walkthrough: Shaggy is Scooby-Doo's companion, so the capital S invites the character, but it is just the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Tufty hair grows in tufts, so it looks shaggy.

clue.text: Prog rockers tense, ready to play song

explanation.surface: A prog rock band, nervous before going on, ready to play their song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' reads as nervous, but it is the grammatical abbreviation T.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Yesterday is the Beatles' famous 1965 ballad.

clue.text: Green and blue uniform scrubbed after a Wren jogged about base

indicators.note: after means following, so BLE is placed behind the other letters

blocks.note: e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: A Wren, a Women's Royal Naval Service sailor, in green and blue kit, runs laps around the naval base.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wren is just letters to rearrange; 'base' is the mathematical constant E.
explanation.definitionFit: Green in its environmental sense: wind and solar are called both green and renewable energy sources.

clue.text: Septuagenarian angry when line is forgotten? It’ll come back

blocks.note: a baby boomer, born after the war and now in their seventies

explanation.surface: An old actor loses his temper when he forgets a line, which will come back to him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line' sounds like a theatre line, but it is a railway, RY.
explanation.definitionFit: A description rather than a synonym: the curved Australian throwing stick is shaped to fly back to the thrower.

clue.text: Kind Arab ruler caught on mike getting something from McDonald’s?

indicators.note: heard, as in catching what someone said

blocks.note: Mike is M in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A kindly sheikh is recorded on a microphone buying a McDonald's meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mike' in the surface is a microphone; it is the NATO alphabet M.
explanation.definitionFit: McDonald's sells milkshakes; the question mark admits it is one example.

clue.text: Glam rock band on blow, heroin and mineral water?

definitions.note: a mud bath is mineral-rich mud rather than water; the question mark flags the stretch

blocks.note: Mud, the 1970s glam rock band of 'Tiger Feet'
to bat is to hit, a blow

explanation.surface: A glam rock band on cocaine, heroin and fizzy water: the rock-star life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow' looks like cocaine next to heroin, but it is BAT, a hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A mud bath is a spa soak in mineral-rich mud.

clue.text: Asda’s 50pc shareholder against online grocer delivering fruit

blocks.note: A is two of the four letters of ASDA: it holds a 50% share
Ocado is a British online supermarket

explanation.surface: Business news: a big Asda shareholder takes on a rival online grocer.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'shareholder' is a letter, not an investor: A makes up half of ASDA. Asda is a British supermarket chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: botanically the avocado is a fruit, a large single-seeded berry, though often eaten like a vegetable.

clue.text: Writer of English/French sea shanty that remains unfinished?

blocks.note: a shanty is a song; SONG loses G

explanation.surface: A writer of a bilingual sea shanty never finishes it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sea shanty' reads as one thing, but 'sea' goes with 'French' to make MER.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Waldo Emerson was the American essayist.

clue.text: Row to one end of river through Swaffham on vacation

indicators.note: passing through something means being inside it

explanation.surface: Rowing to the end of a river through Swaffham, a small Norfolk market town, while on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' reads as rowing a boat; it is a quarrel, the rhyme with 'cow'.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative sense: a storm of protest is a violent public row, as in a storm in a teacup.

clue.text: Crossword setter meets politician to the north of his county seat

blocks.note: the setter refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: The setter meets his local MP up in the county town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'County seat' sounds like a British county town or a parliamentary seat, but it is the US term: Memphis is the seat of Shelby County, Tennessee.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example, in the American sense: a county seat is a county's administrative town, and Memphis, Tennessee, serves Shelby County.

clue.text: Who, say, Solomon’s hit with a golf club?

blocks.note: Doctor Who, the TV time traveller, is a Dr
Solomon is this puzzle's setter, so 'Solomon's' = I've

explanation.surface: Asking who, perhaps Solomon, was struck with a golf club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solomon's' is the setter speaking: Solomon has = I have = I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: A drive is a long shot hit from the tee with a golf club.

clue.text: Old American gangsters may end up here

blocks.note: of the Incas of old Peru
the can is slang for prison

explanation.surface: Old-time American gangsters often finished up in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old American' conjures Prohibition mobsters, but it means Incan, South American.
explanation.definitionFit: The Incan empire was the great pre-Columbian civilisation of South America.

clue.text: Snow under liquid, however, starts to loosen and melt

blocks.note: first letters of loosen and melt

explanation.surface: Snow sitting under water begins to loosen and melt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snow under' looks like snow lying beneath the liquid, but it is the phrasal verb meaning swamp with work.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to snow someone under is to bury them in more work than they can cope with.

clue.text: Faulty Winchester unloaded on top of gunhouse

explanation.surface: A faulty Winchester rifle is unloaded on the roof of the gun turret.
explanation.walkthrough: The rifle, 'unloaded' and gunhouse all build one picture; 'unloaded' actually empties the word itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in the mechanical sense: when a machine is faulty, something is wrong with it.

clue.text: Lost garden gnome finally extracted from shopping centre and returned first-class

indicators.note: A1 is turned back to 1A, read as IA

blocks.note: a shopping arcade; ARCADE loses E
A1 = first-class, with the 1 read as I

explanation.surface: A missing garden gnome turns up in a shopping centre and is sent back first class.
explanation.walkthrough: The gnome gives only its last letter; A1 is written AI, with the digit read as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcadia is the lost pastoral paradise of poets.

clue.text: Someone virtuous and manly moving round belly

explanation.surface: A good, macho man going around with a big belly.
explanation.walkthrough: ST is the standard abbreviation for saint, the crossword's go-to virtuous person.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose everyday synonym: people say stomach for the whole belly, not just the organ.

clue.text: Leave straight after the match

blocks.note: surface: go home at once; meant: leave as time off work, taken immediately
surface: after the game; meant: after the wedding, a match being a marriage

explanation.surface: Heading home as soon as the game ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' suggests sport and 'leave' departing; read them as a wedding and time off work.
explanation.definitionFit: A honeymoon is the holiday newlyweds take right after the wedding.

clue.text: Sizes of plums reduced by 50pc

definitions.note: gage is a variant spelling of gauge

blocks.note: greengages are plums; the first half, GREEN, goes

explanation.surface: A grocer's note that the plums have shrunk by half.
explanation.walkthrough: Gages are themselves plums, which makes 'plums' look like the definition; it is the fodder, and 'Sizes' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Gauges, also spelt gages, are measures of size.
